title: task-specific coordinates in a shared gradient plane
hypothesis: When task update gradients occupy a shared two-dimensional left subspace, a task-specific Givens coordinate plus one rank-1 update vector will retain aligned task quality and prior skills with smaller serialized state than per-task rank-1 LoRA; unrelated update directions will require a larger private basis.
physical_object: One frozen 16x8 base map plus a shared 16x2 orthonormal gradient plane P, charged once
mirror_coordinate: Per-task learned Givens angle in P's two-coordinate plane, paired with one 8D task update vector; the resulting update is (P*[cos(theta),sin(theta)])*v_t^T
logical_multiplicity: Five task-conditioned linear predictors formed from one physical base and four compact gradient-coordinate updates
targeted_literature: FedLore: Communication and Memory Efficient Federated Learning via Shared Gradient Low-Rank Projection (arXiv:2610.01620)
GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection (arXiv:2403.03507)
Orthogonal Gradient Descent for Continual Learning (arXiv:1910.07104)
iGSP: Implicit Gradient Subspace Projection for Efficient Continual Learning of Vision-Language Models (arXiv:2605.19301)
controls: hard-tied base with no task update
ordinary shared-plane rank-2 coefficients C_t in P*C_t (strong generic shared-basis control)
independent full task matrices as upper control
task_stream: Five tasks on 16D inputs and 8D outputs. Task 0 is the common frozen base. Four later task maps are trained sequentially with old task states frozen. In the aligned condition, each delta is a rank-1 update whose left vector lies in the shared plane P. In the independent condition, each task delta is an unrelated dense matrix. Task ID is supplied and stored. The shared plane P is generated per world from a seeded QR basis and fully charged; this screen tests task-code efficiency conditional on a shared gradient plane, not the cost of discovering P from natural data.

development.selection_metric: mean final held-out MSE across all methods and both task conditions, with bytes and retention as preregistered tie-breakers

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes and resumable checkpoint bytes
storage.inference_serialization: deterministic binary tensor records with method, dimensions, task IDs, names, dtypes, shapes, metadata and raw bytes
storage.resume_serialization: torch.save with all current per-task optimizer moments and step counters
paid_objects: each task angle and update vector
all task IDs and record metadata
optimizer states and counters for resume bytes

success_gate: On all three fresh aligned worlds, Mirror final mean task MSE <=1.10x rank-1 LoRA, total inference payload <=0.90x rank-1 LoRA, incremental resume-state bytes per skill <=0.75x rank-1 LoRA, and mean previous-task MSE increase <=0.01. Compare to ordinary shared-plane rank-2 coefficients at actual bytes and compute; if it matches at <= Mirror bytes, do not claim Mirror-specific benefit.
failure_gate: Both development seeds miss either Mirror's quality or total-inference-byte gate versus rank-1 LoRA. Fresh worlds remain sealed on failure.
boundaries: Synthetic linear regression with a supplied shared gradient plane
No discovery cost for the shared basis is inferred from this screen
Independent dense task deltas define the private-capacity boundary
No natural continual-learning or language-model claim
